entry.content:
Pepo Manuchi of Lima, Peru, bought this race-built Cobra early in 1965 and raced it hard, often over long distances from one Peruvian city to the next. Shelby built only 23 full-competition 427 Cobras, and CSX3029 is the 23rd. More than 100 factory changes set it apart from a standard Competition 427, among them a roll bar, side pipes, a big 42-gallon tank and an oil cooler for the differential. A 427-cubic-inch Ford V8 makes 606 horsepower in a car that weighs only about 2,400 pounds, impressively light for that level of power.

entry.content:
The Fabric of the Game, a film by The Old Ghosts and Titleist, heads to Scotland to find where golf, tartan and tweed meet. It begins at the Harris Tweed Hebrides mill in the Outer Hebrides, where Margaret Ann Macleod and Mark Hogarth walk the crew through how Harris Tweed is made. British wool gets dyed in Titleist's colors, spun into yarn and sent out to a weaver working at home, who makes a Titleist tartan from it, officially added to the Scottish Register of Tartans. Next, John Sugden of Campbell's of Beauly explains how tweed is tied to the land, Iona Stephen in St Andrews shows how tweed and golf are bound together, and headcover maker Robbie Spriddle of Hame stops for a pint in Kingsbarns. The island mills, the Isle of Harris Golf Club, and the Highlands also make appearances in this short film, where each frame demonstrates how the browns and greens of Scottish tweed emulate the rich landscape.

entry.content:
Yarbo takes the work out of winter maintenance with an autonomous robotic snow blower designed to keep driveways and sidewalks clear around the clock. Capable of clearing up to 12 inches of dry, fluffy snow in a single pass, it can also be outfitted with a dedicated plow blade to handle heavier, wetter conditions. The robot plans its own routes, clears snow automatically, and returns to its charging dock when battery levels drop below 20%, resuming work once recharged. Through the Yarbo app, homeowners can schedule tasks, monitor progress, and manage operations remotely, while advanced obstacle detection helps identify people, pets, and vehicles. Best of all, the modular platform works beyond winter, swapping attachments for lawn mowing, trimming, and leaf blowing throughout the year. With Black Friday savings of up to $2,500, there's never been a better time to put property maintenance on autopilot.

entry.content:
Honda builds the Africa Twin for three kinds of rides in 2027. The standard bike keeps a 21-inch front wheel. The Adventure Sports, made for long distances, moves to a 19-inch wheel and a bigger tank that stretches the miles between fuel stops. An Adventure Sports version with Honda SENSING RIDE has radar at the front and rear that keeps a set distance from traffic ahead, even in stop-and-go, and warns riders about vehicles in their blind spot. The new Enduro Sports goes the other way, taking its longer-travel suspension and styling from the CRF450 Rally racer to handle rough ground.

The Moon Shoe took its nickname in 1971, after runners decided the prints it left across the track resembled footsteps on the moon. Back when the company had no name yet, Bill Bowerman made the brand's first running shoe with his wife's waffle iron, and this OG brings the design back in a low-profile build: a nylon upper, a leather Swoosh and a waffle sole. Available in Anthracite, Vintage Green, Black and Tough Red.

entry.content:
In 1901, Henry Ford, a first-time racer with little chance on paper, drove his own two-cylinder car around a dirt track near Detroit and won cash and a glass punchbowl. The 2028 Mustang GTD 1901 honors that car, called Sweepstakes, with paint in Deep Royal Red, a black racing stripe off to one side and a red centerline, a nod to the original's red frame and black body. The seats are Mahogany Red leather with Race Red stitching, and optional titanium trim is printed from metal salvaged from retired F-22 jets. The GTD is Ford's fastest factory-built Mustang, with a 5.2-liter supercharged V8 making as much as 815 horsepower.

entry.summary: Titaner's Monolith lighter has a refillable butane core covered by a shell cut from the Muonionalusta meteorite, an iron rock that hit northern Sweden a million years back. The cutting and finishing process brings out a crisscross crystal pattern that Titaner says no machine can
entry.content:
Titaner's Monolith lighter has a refillable butane core covered by a shell cut from the Muonionalusta meteorite, an iron rock that hit northern Sweden a million years back. The cutting and finishing process brings out a crisscross crystal pattern that Titaner says no machine can copy, so every lighter looks different. A copper heat sink pulls heat away from the fuel core, and the vents echo Li, the I Ching trigram for fire, light and clarity. A magnetic slide at the base opens the refill valve and hides a spare flint. The name is a reference to the black slab in 2001: A Space Odyssey.

entry.content:
Skepta spent 18 months at Classic Works, Land Rover's workshop in Ryton-on-Dunsmore, England, where specialists restore and upgrade Defenders by hand. The result is a Defender 110 pickup, remade into a one-of-one build that carries Skepta's own stamp, including a custom bed cover that doubles as a platform for DJ gear. The bronze paint looks nearly black in dim light, and a black roof and arches add contrast. The cabin is two-tone red and ebony, the red referencing his children's shoes. His fashion label, MAINS, shows up on the headrests, the debossed logos and the wheel center caps.

entry.summary: Rolls-Royce puts its luxury spin on the 5,000-year-old game of backgammon. The set opens on a machined aluminum hinge, and as the case swings open, the center spine turns the opposite way, revealing the board, while a Spirit of Ecstasy keeps itself upright wherever the hinge land
entry.content:
Rolls-Royce puts its luxury spin on the 5,000-year-old game of backgammon. The set opens on a machined aluminum hinge, and as the case swings open, the center spine turns the opposite way, revealing the board, while a Spirit of Ecstasy keeps itself upright wherever the hinge lands. The board is solid American walnut, with points inlaid in walnut and eucalyptus, and the case is trimmed in Sunset and Sunrise Rolls-Royce natural grain leather. The same spine tucks away the black and white stones. Even the doubling die breaks from tradition: a hexagon instead of a cube, it draws on honeycombs in nature and the exactness of nuts and bolts, and it echoes the apiaries the company runs from Goodwood to Doha. Clients commission one through Rolls-Royce's Private Office boutiques and showrooms.
